question: Who took away the Peacock Throne from India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nadir Shah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Peacock Throne was commissioned by ​Shah Jahan in the early 17th century.
 
• It was the seat of Mughal Emperors in India and was placed in the **Diwan-i-Khas** in the Red Fort of Delhi.
 
• When Nadir shah attacked and looted India in 1739, he also took the precious throne with him.
 
• The Peacock Throne was covered in gold and jewels, with steps leading up to it, with the ruler floating above the ground.
 
• The opulence and magnificence can be estimated from the fact that it cost twice as much as the construction of the majestic Taj Mahal.
 
• The peacock throne had the famous Koh-I-Noor diamond embedded in it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Nadir Shah**

 
 
• Nadir Shah invaded India in the year 1739.
 
• He defeated the Mughal Emperor Muhammad Shah in the Battle of Karnal and plundered Delhi, taking immense wealth, including the Kohinoor diamond and the Peacock Throne.
 
 
 
• **Genghis Khan**
 
 
• Genghis Khan, original name Temüjin, (born 1162, near Lake Baikal, Mongolia—died August 18, 1227), was a Mongolian warrior-ruler, one of the most famous conquerors of history, who consolidated tribes into a unified Mongolia.
 
• Genghis Khan died in 1227, having spent most of his life in military combat.
 
• His military achievements were astounding and they were largely a result of his ability to innovate and transform different aspects of steppe combat into extremely effective military strategies. 
 
• Between 18 to Aug. 25, 1227, during Genghis Khan's last campaign against the Western Xia, he felt unwell with a fever that ultimately killed him within eight days after the disease's onset.
 
• Thus, Genghis Khan died in 1227CE.
 
 
 
• **​Mohammad bin Tuglaq**
 
 
• **Mohammad bin Tughlaq**__ holds the title of Amir ul Momineen.
 
• Mohammad bin Tughlaq was the** son of Gaiyasuddin Tuglaq.**
 
• His original name was **Juna Khan**.
 
• Mohammad bin Tughlaq has good knowledge of Arabic, Persian, Mathematics, Astronomy, Physics and Medical science.
 
• Mohammad bin Tughlaq is considered as three-star wonderer or wise fool by historians.
 
 
 
• **Ahmed Shah**
 
 
• Ahmad shah (1748-1754), the only son of Muhammad Shah, succeeded his father after his death.
 
• He was mostly engaged in irrelevant activities, giving very little attention and time to the affairs of state that caused weakening defences at North-west and allowed Abdali to invade in 1748 AD.
 
• He handed the affairs of the state to his mother Udham Bai who acted as a regent under her son Ahmad Shah.
 
• Udham Bai did not possess the intellect required to run the empire efficiently and hence, the Mughal state started declining rapidly.
 
• When Ahmad Shah ascended the throne at Delhi in 1748, Safdarjung became his Wazir or Vizier or Prime Minister of the empire.
 
• Safdarjung was an able administrator and was a major figure at the Mughal court.
 
• He became the second Nawab of Awadh when he succeeded Saadat Ali Khan I in 1739 AD.
 
• 
 
It was during his time that the Lucknow culture developed around Awadh.
